contentMarkdown:
# Resolución Forense: Enrutamiento Multi-Tenant, Loopback y Resincronización Nginx

Este informe documenta la investigación técnica exhaustiva, el análisis de causa raíz a nivel del código fuente interno de **Next.js 16 Standalone**, la discrepancia en la normalización de sockets loopback en Linux y la solución arquitectónica definitiva que restauró el 100% de la operatividad en producción para el ecosistema multi-dominio en un servidor **AWS Lightsail con 1 GB de RAM (Debian 13)**.

---

## 1. Resumen Ejecutivo y Ficha Técnica del Incidente (P1)

| Parámetro | Valor y Detalle en Producción |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Fecha de Ocurrencia** | 8 – 9 de Septiembre de 2026 |
| **Severidad Operativa** | **P1 (Crítico)** — Todos los subdominios caídos |
| **Servicios Afectados** | `bible.jorgedoicela.com`, `portfolio.jorgedoicela.com`, `software.jorgedoicela.com` |
| **Servicio No Afectado** | `jorgedoicela.com` (Landing Page en dominio raíz) |
| **Impacto en el Usuario** | `HTTP 500 Internal Server Error` en navegadores y llamadas cURL |
| **Firma del Error en Logs** | `Error: write EPROTO: SSL routines: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER` en `proxy-request.js` |
| **Causa Raíz** | Inconsistencia interna en Next.js 16 Standalone entre `opts.hostname` en `resolve-routes.js` y la normalización de loopback de `NextURL` (`REGEX_LOCALHOST_HOSTNAME`), lo cual convertía las reescrituras de subdominios (`middleware.ts`) en llamadas de proxy externo hacia su propio socket HTTP plano mediante HTTPS |
| **Resolución** | **Desacoplamiento Dual-Stack**: Next.js en IPv6 loopback (`[::1]:3001` vía `HOSTNAME: 'localhost'`), NestJS en IPv4 loopback (`127.0.0.1:3000`), y upstream dinámico Nginx |

---

## 2. El Vector de Origen: Hardening Perimetral y Defensa en Profundidad

Durante la auditoría de seguridad del servidor Debian 13, se descubrió que los procesos Node.js escuchaban de forma predeterminada en todas las interfaces de red (`0.0.0.0:3000` y `0.0.0.0:3001`). Esto significaba que cualquier atacante que conociera la IP pública del VPS podía conectarse directamente a los puertos de las aplicaciones, **bypasseando el proxy inverso Nginx y la autenticación mutua TLS (mTLS) de Cloudflare**.

Para implementar el principio de *Defensa en Profundidad*, se ejecutaron dos acciones correctivas inmediatas:
1. **Firewall del Sistema Operativo (UFW):** Establecer política por defecto `DROP` en tráfico entrante y permitir únicamente los puertos 22 (SSH), 80 (HTTP) y 443 (HTTPS mTLS).
2. **Bind Local de Procesos:** Forzar a Node.js a escuchar exclusivamente en loopback local en `pm2.config.js`:

```javascript
// Configuración inicial de intento de hardening (Causante del Incidente)
{
  name: 'backend-nest',
  env: { HOST: '127.0.0.1', PORT: 3000 }
},
{
  name: 'frontend-next',
  env: { HOSTNAME: '127.0.0.1', PORT: 3001 }
}
```

---

## 3. El Colapso Inmediato y los Síntomas Forenses

Al reiniciar los procesos con PM2, ocurrió un fenómeno desconcertante:
* La **Landing Page (`jorgedoicela.com`)** continuó respondiendo `HTTP 200 OK` de manera impecable.
* Sin embargo, **todos los subdominios** (`bible`, `portfolio`, `software`) comenzaron a fallar instantáneamente con `HTTP 500 Internal Server Error`.

Al inspeccionar los logs de error de PM2 (`~/.pm2/logs/frontend-next-error.log`), se registraron múltiples trazas del siguiente error crítico:

```text
Failed to proxy https://localhost:3001/software Error: write EPROTO 80F2CC34637F0000:error:0A00010B:SSL routines:tls_validate_record_header:wrong version number:../deps/openssl/openssl/ssl/record/methods/tlsany_meth.c:77:
    at ignore-listed frames {
  errno: -71,
  code: 'EPROTO',
  syscall: 'write'
}
```

¿Por qué el servidor intentaba actuar como un cliente HTTPS contra `localhost:3001` si era él mismo quien servía la petición por HTTP plano?

---

## 4. Descenso Forense al Código Fuente de Next.js 16 Standalone

Para identificar la causa raíz real sin aplicar parches ni conjeturas, se inspeccionaron los archivos fuente compilados dentro de `node_modules/next/dist/server/`:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Cliente as Cliente / Navegador
    participant Nginx as Nginx Reverse Proxy (:443)
    participant Next as Next.js Standalone (:3001)
    participant Socket as Socket Local (127.0.0.1:3001)

    Cliente->>Nginx: Petición HTTPS (subdominio)
    Nginx->>Next: proxy_pass con X-Forwarded-Proto: https
    Note over Next: resolve-routes.js construye initUrl = https://127.0.0.1:3001/
    Note over Next: NextURL fuerza hostname a localhost
    Next->>Next: relativize-url.js (127.0.0.1 !== localhost - Relatividad Falsa)
    Next->>Socket: router-server.js dispara proxyRequest() TLS sobre HTTP
    Socket-->>Next: Fallo SSL Handshake: Error write EPROTO (HTTP 500)
    Next-->>Cliente: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
```

### 4.1 La Construcción de la URL Base en `resolve-routes.js`
En `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-utils/resolve-routes.js` (Líneas 114–116):
```javascript
const protocol = (req?.socket?.encrypted) || (req.headers['x-forwarded-proto']?.includes('https')) ? 'https' : 'http';

const initUrl = config.experimental.trustHostHeader 
  ? `https://${req.headers.host || 'localhost'}${req.url}` 
  : opts.port 
    ? `${protocol}://${formatHostname(opts.hostname || 'localhost')}:${opts.port}${req.url}` 
    : req.url || '';
```
1. Como Nginx recibe tráfico SSL y envía `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, la variable `protocol` se fijaba en `'https'`.
2. Como se configuró `HOSTNAME: '127.0.0.1'`, `opts.hostname` tomó el valor literal `'127.0.0.1'`.
3. `initUrl` se calculó como:
   `initUrl = https://127.0.0.1:3001/`

### 4.2 La Normalización Oculta de `NextURL` en `next-url.js`
En `node_modules/next/dist/server/web/next-url.js` (Líneas 14–21):
```javascript
const REGEX_LOCALHOST_HOSTNAME = /^(?:127(?:\.(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)){3}|\[::1\]|localhost)$/;

function parseURL(url, base) {
    const parsed = new URL(String(url), base && String(base));
    if (REGEX_LOCALHOST_HOSTNAME.test(parsed.hostname)) {
        parsed.hostname = 'localhost'; // <-- Mutación forzada a 'localhost'
    }
    return parsed;
}
```
Cuando `src/middleware.ts` evalúa el subdominio (`request.nextUrl`), la expresión regular intercepta `127.0.0.1` y **lo reemplaza arbitrariamente por `'localhost'`**.
Por lo tanto, la cabecera interna de reescritura emitida por el middleware fue:
`x-middleware-rewrite = https://localhost:3001/software`

### 4.3 El Juicio de Relatividad en `relativize-url.js`
En `node_modules/next/dist/shared/lib/router/utils/relativize-url.js`:
```javascript
function parseRelativeURL(url, base) {
    const baseURL = typeof base === 'string' ? new URL(base) : base;
    const relative = new URL(url, base);
    const isRelative = relative.origin === baseURL.origin;
    return {
        url: isRelative ? relative.toString().slice(baseURL.origin.length) : relative.toString(),
        isRelative
    };
}
```
El router compara los orígenes:
* `baseURL.origin` → `https://127.0.0.1:3001` (proveniente de `initUrl`).
* `relative.origin` → `https://localhost:3001` (proveniente de `NextURL`).
* **¿`baseURL.origin === relative.origin`?** → `false`.

### 4.4 El Disparo Fatal de `proxyRequest` en `router-server.js`
Al fallar la comprobación de igualdad de cadenas, Next.js concluyó que la petición debía redirigirse a un servidor externo:
```javascript
if (finished && parsedUrl.protocol) {
    return await proxyRequest(req, res, parsedUrl, ...);
}
```
`proxyRequest` abrió un socket saliente cliente con TLS hacia `https://localhost:3001`. Como el puerto 3001 de Next.js es un servidor HTTP estándar sin cifrado local, la negociación de apretón de manos SSL falló con `EPROTO wrong version number` y abortó la conexión con HTTP 500.

---

## 5. El Comportamiento Dual de Red en Debian 13 (La Trampa IPv4 vs IPv6)

Para subsanar la discrepancia de cadenas de origen, la solución conceptual inmediata era configurar `HOSTNAME: 'localhost'` en PM2, alineando `opts.hostname` con `NextURL`.

Sin embargo, al aplicar este cambio emergió un segundo problema de infraestructura:
1. En Linux moderno (Debian 13 Trixie), el resolver del sistema (`getaddrinfo`) mapea el nombre `localhost` prioritariamente a la dirección **IPv6 loopback (`::1`)**.
2. En consecuencia, el servidor Next.js se levantó escuchando en:
   ```text
   LISTEN 0 511 [::1]:3001 [::]:* users:(("next-server",pid=1649,fd=23))
   ```
3. La configuración existente de Nginx en `/etc/nginx/sites-available/jorgedoicela.com.conf` contenía:
   ```nginx
   proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3001; # <-- Dirección IPv4
   ```
4. Nginx intentaba comunicarse con `127.0.0.1:3001`, pero en ese socket IPv4 ya no había nadie escuchando. El kernel devolvía de inmediato `ECONNREFUSED (111: Connection refused)` y Nginx respondía al cliente con `HTTP 502 Bad Gateway`.

---

## 6. La Solución Arquitectónica Definitiva (Cero Parches, 100% Robusta)

La solución correcta no requirió modificar el código del framework ni vulnerar la seguridad del servidor con variables experimentales no probadas. Se implementó una arquitectura limpia de 3 pilares:

### Pilar 1: Orquestación en PM2 (`pm2.config.js`)
Se declaró explícitamente el protocolo de enlace de red para cada runtime:
```javascript
module.exports = {
  apps: [
    {
      name: 'backend-nest',
      script: './dist/main.js',
      cwd: './backend',
      instances: 1,
      exec_mode: 'fork',
      max_memory_restart: '200M',
      env: {
        NODE_ENV: 'production',
        HOST: '127.0.0.1', // Sella el socket a IPv4 loopback puro para SQLite y REST
        PORT: 3000
      }
    },
    {
      name: 'frontend-next',
      script: './server.js',
      cwd: './frontend/web/.next/standalone/frontend/web',
      instances: 1,
      exec_mode: 'fork',
      max_memory_restart: '200M',
      env: {
        NODE_ENV: 'production',
        PORT: 3001,
        HOSTNAME: 'localhost' // Sella a IPv6 loopback [::1], 100% alineado con NextURL
      }
    }
  ]
};
```

### Pilar 2: Enrutador Nginx con Upstream Dual (`nginx/jorgedoicela.com.conf`)
Nginx fue reconfigurado para comunicarse directamente con el socket IPv6 para Next.js y el socket IPv4 para NestJS:
```nginx
# Enrutamiento dinámico de alto rendimiento
map $http_accept $backend_upstream {
    default                 http://127.0.0.1:3000; # Backend NestJS (IPv4)
    ~*text/html             http://[::1]:3001;     # Frontend Next.js (IPv6)
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    listen [::]:443 ssl;
    server_name jorgedoicela.com *.jorgedoicela.com;

    # Frontend Web SSR / RSC
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://[::1]:3001;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade';
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $http_cf_connecting_ip;
    }

    # API REST NestJS
    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}
```

### Pilar 3: Blindaje en Kernel con UFW Netfilter y Cloudflare mTLS
```bash
# Sellar puertos 3000 y 3001 a nivel de tarjeta de red eth0
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp comment 'SSH fail2ban'
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp comment 'HTTP redirect'
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp comment 'HTTPS Cloudflare mTLS'
sudo ufw enable
```

---

## 7. Verificación Empírica y Telemetría Post-Incidente

Tras aplicar la arquitectura dual, se ejecutaron pruebas forenses de verificación desde el exterior y en el host local:

```bash
# 1. Comprobación de códigos de estado HTTP en todos los dominios
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "Landing (jorgedoicela.com): %{http_code}
" https://jorgedoicela.com/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "Biblia (bible.*): %{http_code}
" https://bible.jorgedoicela.com/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "Software (software.*): %{http_code}
" https://software.jorgedoicela.com/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "Portafolio (portfolio.*): %{http_code}
" https://portfolio.jorgedoicela.com/
```

**Salida de terminal verificada:**
```text
Landing (jorgedoicela.com): 200
Biblia (bible.*): 200
Software (software.*): 200
Portafolio (portfolio.*): 200
```

**Inspección de sockets locales (`ss -tlnp`):**
```text
LISTEN  127.0.0.1:3000   users:(("node",pid=320236,fd=32))        <-- NestJS (IPv4 Loopback)
LISTEN  [::1]:3001       users:(("next-server",pid=1649,fd=23))    <-- Next.js (IPv6 Loopback)
```

**Telemetría de memoria en el VPS de 1 GB RAM:**
* Consumo total de RAM: **496 MB / 939 MB (52.5%)** — estado perfectamente estable y saludable.
* Reinicios de PM2: **0 reinicios** acumulados tras la estabilización.

---

## 8. Lecciones de Arquitectura y Reglas de Oro

1. **Evitar parches en capas intermedias:** Intentar mitigar el problema falsificando cabeceras `Host` o manipulando flags experimentales como `trustHostHeader` introduce comportamientos erráticos en el router. Las causas raíz deben resolverse en el punto exacto de discordancia.
2. **Entender la semántica de red del framework:** En Next.js Standalone, `HOSTNAME` no es un simple parámetro de enlace de red de bajo nivel, sino que altera la semántica de origen canónico utilizada para evaluar la relatividad de las reescrituras de middleware.
3. **El Kernel como primera barrera:** La seguridad perimetral debe ser delegada al firewall del sistema operativo (UFW/Netfilter) y a la autenticación mutua TLS (mTLS). El bind a loopback en Node.js es una valiosa segunda línea de defensa, pero debe diseñarse en perfecta armonía con el router interno de la aplicación.

# Forensic Resolution: Multi-Tenant Routing, Loopback Sockets, and Nginx Resynchronization

This incident report provides an exhaustive technical postmortem, source code root cause analysis inside **Next.js 16 Standalone**, socket loopback discrepancies in modern Linux, and the definitive architectural solution restoring 100% operational uptime on an **AWS Lightsail 1 GB RAM VPS (Debian 13)**.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Incident Facts (P1)

| Parameter | Production Value & Analysis |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Incident Date** | September 8 – 9, 2026 |
| **Severity** | **P1 (Critical Outage)** — All multi-tenant subdomains down |
| **Impacted Services** | `bible.jorgedoicela.com`, `portfolio.jorgedoicela.com`, `software.jorgedoicela.com` |
| **Unaffected Service** | `jorgedoicela.com` (Root Domain Landing Page) |
| **User Symptom** | `HTTP 500 Internal Server Error` on browser and cURL calls |
| **Error Signature in Logs** | `Error: write EPROTO: SSL routines: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER` inside `proxy-request.js` |
| **Root Cause** | Internal discrepancy in Next.js 16 Standalone between `opts.hostname` in `resolve-routes.js` and `NextURL` loopback regex (`REGEX_LOCALHOST_HOSTNAME`), converting subdomain middleware rewrites into outbound external proxy calls using HTTPS against its own plaintext HTTP port |
| **Resolution** | **Dual-Stack Decoupling**: Next.js on IPv6 loopback (`[::1]:3001` via `HOSTNAME: 'localhost'`), NestJS on IPv4 loopback (`127.0.0.1:3000`), and Nginx dynamic upstream routing |

---

## 2. Trigger Event: Perimeter Hardening and Defense in Depth

During a server security audit on Debian 13, audit scans revealed that Node.js processes were listening on wildcard addresses (`0.0.0.0:3000` and `0.0.0.0:3001`). Anyone possessing the VPS public IP could access application ports directly, **bypassing Nginx reverse proxy policies and Cloudflare Mutual TLS (mTLS)**.

To enforce *Defense in Depth*, two immediate remediations were initiated:
1. **OS Firewall (UFW):** Setting default incoming policy to `DROP`, allowing only ports 22 (SSH), 80 (HTTP), and 443 (HTTPS mTLS).
2. **Local Socket Binding:** Restricting Node.js processes to loopback interfaces in `pm2.config.js`:

```javascript
// Initial naive hardening attempt (Triggered the Outage)
{
  name: 'backend-nest',
  env: { HOST: '127.0.0.1', PORT: 3000 }
},
{
  name: 'frontend-next',
  env: { HOSTNAME: '127.0.0.1', PORT: 3001 }
}
```

---

## 3. The Immediate Outage and Forensic Symptoms

Upon reloading PM2:
* The **Landing Page (`jorgedoicela.com`)** continued to return `HTTP 200 OK` seamlessly because it does not require subdomain rewrites in `middleware.ts`.
* In contrast, **all subdomains** (`bible`, `portfolio`, `software`) immediately failed with `HTTP 500 Internal Server Error`.

PM2 error logs (`~/.pm2/logs/frontend-next-error.log`) revealed repetitive fatal exceptions:

```text
Failed to proxy https://localhost:3001/software Error: write EPROTO 80F2CC34637F0000:error:0A00010B:SSL routines:tls_validate_record_header:wrong version number:../deps/openssl/openssl/ssl/record/methods/tlsany_meth.c:77:
    at ignore-listed frames {
  errno: -71,
  code: 'EPROTO',
  syscall: 'write'
}
```

Why was the server attempting an outbound HTTPS proxy connection against `localhost:3001` while serving a plaintext HTTP socket?

---

## 4. Deep-Dive Forensic Source Code Audit of Next.js 16 Standalone

To find the true root cause without hacks or workarounds, the compiled runtime code in `node_modules/next/dist/server/` was investigated:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Client as Client / Browser
    participant Nginx as Nginx Reverse Proxy (:443)
    participant Next as Next.js Standalone (:3001)
    participant Socket as Local Socket (127.0.0.1:3001)

    Client->>Nginx: HTTPS Request (subdomain)
    Nginx->>Next: proxy_pass with X-Forwarded-Proto: https
    Note over Next: resolve-routes.js builds initUrl = https://127.0.0.1:3001/
    Note over Next: NextURL normalizes hostname to localhost
    Next->>Next: relativize-url.js (127.0.0.1 !== localhost - Non-relative)
    Next->>Socket: router-server.js triggers proxyRequest() TLS over HTTP
    Socket-->>Next: SSL Handshake Crash: Error write EPROTO (HTTP 500)
    Next-->>Client: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
```

### 4.1 Base URL Construction in `resolve-routes.js`
Inside `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-utils/resolve-routes.js` (Lines 114–116):
```javascript
const protocol = (req?.socket?.encrypted) || (req.headers['x-forwarded-proto']?.includes('https')) ? 'https' : 'http';

const initUrl = config.experimental.trustHostHeader 
  ? `https://${req.headers.host || 'localhost'}${req.url}` 
  : opts.port 
    ? `${protocol}://${formatHostname(opts.hostname || 'localhost')}:${opts.port}${req.url}` 
    : req.url || '';
```
1. Because Nginx terminates SSL and forwards `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, `protocol` evaluates to `'https'`.
2. Because `HOSTNAME: '127.0.0.1'` was configured in PM2, `opts.hostname` evaluated to `'127.0.0.1'`.
3. `initUrl` was synthesized as:
   `initUrl = https://127.0.0.1:3001/`

### 4.2 The Hidden Normalization of `NextURL` in `next-url.js`
Inside `node_modules/next/dist/server/web/next-url.js` (Lines 14–21):
```javascript
const REGEX_LOCALHOST_HOSTNAME = /^(?:127(?:\.(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)){3}|\[::1\]|localhost)$/;

function parseURL(url, base) {
    const parsed = new URL(String(url), base && String(base));
    if (REGEX_LOCALHOST_HOSTNAME.test(parsed.hostname)) {
        parsed.hostname = 'localhost'; // <-- Mutates hostname to 'localhost'
    }
    return parsed;
}
```
When `src/middleware.ts` parses the incoming request via `NextRequest`, the regex matches `127.0.0.1` and **forces it to `'localhost'`**.
Consequently, the rewrite header emitted was:
`x-middleware-rewrite = https://localhost:3001/software`

### 4.3 Relativity Evaluation in `relativize-url.js`
Inside `node_modules/next/dist/shared/lib/router/utils/relativize-url.js`:
```javascript
function parseRelativeURL(url, base) {
    const baseURL = typeof base === 'string' ? new URL(base) : base;
    const relative = new URL(url, base);
    const isRelative = relative.origin === baseURL.origin;
    return {
        url: isRelative ? relative.toString().slice(baseURL.origin.length) : relative.toString(),
        isRelative
    };
}
```
The router compares origins:
* `baseURL.origin` → `https://127.0.0.1:3001` (from `initUrl`).
* `relative.origin` → `https://localhost:3001` (from `NextURL`).
* **Does `baseURL.origin === relative.origin`?** → `false`.

### 4.4 Fatal Execution of `proxyRequest` in `router-server.js`
Because the URL was deemed absolute and non-relative, Next.js attempted external proxy dispatch:
```javascript
if (finished && parsedUrl.protocol) {
    return await proxyRequest(req, res, parsedUrl, ...);
}
```
`proxyRequest` opened an outbound client TLS connection to `https://localhost:3001`. Since Next.js port 3001 is a plaintext HTTP server, the TLS handshake aborted with `EPROTO wrong version number`, failing with HTTP 500.

---

## 5. Linux Dual-Stack Trap in Debian 13 (IPv4 vs IPv6)

To resolve the string origin mismatch, configuring `HOSTNAME: 'localhost'` in PM2 aligns `opts.hostname` with `NextURL`.

However, on modern Linux distributions like Debian 13, a second network obstacle appeared:
1. Node.js on Linux resolves `localhost` via system resolver `getaddrinfo` prioritizing **IPv6 loopback (`::1`)**.
2. As a result, Next.js opened its listening socket on:
   ```text
   LISTEN 0 511 [::1]:3001 [::]:* users:(("next-server",pid=1649,fd=23))
   ```
3. Nginx configuration had:
   ```nginx
   proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3001; # <-- IPv4 address
   ```
4. Nginx attempted connecting to `127.0.0.1:3001`, but no process was listening on IPv4 port 3001. The kernel returned `ECONNREFUSED (111: Connection refused)`, yielding `HTTP 502 Bad Gateway`.

---

## 6. The Production Architectural Solution (Zero Patches)

The permanent solution required zero monkey-patching or experimental flags. A clean three-pillar architecture was deployed:

### Pillar 1: PM2 Dual-Stack Ecosystem (`pm2.config.js`)
Explicitly specifying network bindings per service:
```javascript
module.exports = {
  apps: [
    {
      name: 'backend-nest',
      script: './dist/main.js',
      cwd: './backend',
      instances: 1,
      exec_mode: 'fork',
      max_memory_restart: '200M',
      env: {
```

### Pillar 2: Dynamic Nginx Upstream (`nginx/jorgedoicela.com.conf`)
```nginx
map $http_accept $backend_upstream {
    default                 http://127.0.0.1:3000; # NestJS API (IPv4)
    ~*text/html             http://[::1]:3001;     # Next.js Web (IPv6)
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    listen [::]:443 ssl;
    server_name jorgedoicela.com *.jorgedoicela.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://[::1]:3001;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade';
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $http_cf_connecting_ip;
    }

    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}
```

## 8. Architectural Rules and Key Takeaways

1. **Avoid Middle-Layer Hacks:** Do not attempt header spoofing or unstable experimental flags. Address root causes at their origin.
2. **Framework Network Semantics:** In Next.js Standalone, `HOSTNAME` defines both network socket binding and canonical origin semantics used by internal middleware rewrite relativization logic.
3. **Kernel as First Line of Defense:** Hardware/kernel perimeter security (UFW Netfilter) and authenticated origin pulls (mTLS) remain non-negotiable. Application loopback binding acts as defense in depth.
